pin_added.question: What happens when the sanctions screen gets a hit?
Can a reviewer refuse, or only approve?
Does the two-day sweep ever stop?

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Self-service. The client keys their own details, so the data arrives structured but unverified.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: A monitored mailbox. Free-form: somebody has to read it and transcribe it, which is where a keying error would enter.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: A relationship manager enters it by hand on the client's behalf. The only route where the client never touches the form.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**Every route funnels through here.** All three sources are logged before anything else happens, which makes this the first point where a request exists as a record.

For compliance this is the provenance point: after this box the three routes are indistinguishable unless the log records which one it came from.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Drawn as pass-through, because that is how it was described. **No failure exit is drawn** — see the pinned question on the sanctions screen; the same gap applies here.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
Drawn as pass-through: everything reaching it continues to risk banding.

**This is almost certainly incomplete.** A sanctions hit normally stops a request where it stands rather than banding it. Pinned.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**The only branch in the pipeline.** Three ways out: straight through, needs review, refuse.

Drawn taller than its neighbours because it is the decision the whole flow turns on.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
Sweeps once a day. Anything sitting in manual review more than two days is pushed back to banding.

Drawn as a loop back into banding, which is what was described — note that means a request can be re-banded repeatedly. Pinned.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
A human looks at the case.

Deliberately **not** called a review queue: Argus already has a *Review queue* for sub-threshold Signals and the two are unrelated. Same word, different system.

Only one exit is drawn — approved. Whether a reviewer can also refuse is pinned.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: Where straight-through and reviewed cases converge. From here the two are treated identically.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: First money in. Drawn as a single step; whether it can fail or part-fund is not described.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: The end of the happy path — the client is on board.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip:
**The audit trail for a refusal.** Distinct from the letter on purpose: the log is the record that survives, the letter is what the client receives.

Compliance will ask what is retained here and for how long. Nothing in this drawing answers that.

customData.author: agent
customData.tooltip: What the client is told. No path returns from here — a refusal is drawn as final, with no appeal route.
